task: ADR-011 (Project Tailoring and Route Decision, short form): approve, reject, or request revision

criteria.description: A route per management plan decided by a human with the system recommending; floors and caps as flags with recommendation and decision both recorded; Charter-set limits with the integration section in the Charter or PMP; Stage 17 and Stage 18 change paths; remedial breakouts. Consistent with ADR-001, ADR-002, ADR-003, ADR-008 and ADR-009. Known weaknesses: five decisions in one ADR, Decision 3 bundles several concepts, approve-pmp is not built, PMBOK 8 mapping rests on excerpts.

Four alternatives named and rejected with reasons (full suite always, agent-inferred route, system-enforced blocks, ad hoc tailoring with no record); terse, and the hard-rule question for cost, scope and schedule is left open rather than argued.

Consequences name reliance on the team acting on flags, the bundling in Decision 3 and the need for later ADRs; honest but light, with little on cost of the added Charter and integration-section ceremony.

Unbuilt approve-pmp, the unresolved depths, hard-rule question, per-element question and Stage 17 approval route are stated; most detail is deferred to working notes rather than in the ADR, and the PMBOK 6th-versus-8th numbering mismatch is only in the notes.

evidence.source: direct_doc_read:docs/adr/ADR-011-project-tailoring-and-route-decision.md; cross-checked against ADR-001, ADR-002, ADR-003, ADR-008, ADR-009
